- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk aversion or market panic.
- Model consistently overpredicts prices in the first 5–7 days of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; apply downward bias to early forecast points.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overreacts and forecasts continued rise; cap forecast at 1–2 days above true peak, then allow gradual mean reversion.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.8 to -0.4), model fails to adjust quickly; reduce forecast slope and add early mean-reversion term.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is low but price is trending up; increase forecast by 1–2% to compensate for sentiment lag.
- For 30-day horizon, if last 3–5 days of sentiment are neutral or slightly negative, model tends to underestimate; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to compensate for mean reversion bias.
